FOREWORD

This Indian Standard ( Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Agricultural Tractors and Power Tillers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture DIvision Council Agncultural tractors are basically meant for field operations like ploughmg, cultivation, harrowing, etc and haulage of agricultural produce and their residues Therefore, It is very important that tractors perform well in the field operations and haulage and It necessitated the formulation of gutdetmes for field performance and haulage tests of agricultural tractors
In

This standard was first published in 1979 and subsequently revised In 1987 Based on the experience gamed the use of this standard by the Central Farm Machinery Trammg and Testing Institute, Budru, a need was felt to revise It egam This revrston includes the fotlowmg major changes! addtnons
a)

Classification offield operations have been modified, Duration of field performance test has been reduced from 150 h to 75 h; Recommended moisture content as well as classification of SOIl have been modified; Recommended speeds for various field operations have been incorporated for guidance, Recommended throttle settings have been modified fOT field tests;

b)
c) d)

e)
f)

Requirements for test track for haulage test have been

specified, and

g)

Total distance for haulage test have been changed from 'up to 100 km ' to 'minimum 60 km '

Field performance of the tractors vary with the field conditions It IS, therefore, recommended that the test results obtained under different condmons shall not taken into consideration for evaluatmg the comparative field performance of tractors

In repornng the result of a test. made m accordance with thts standard if the final value, observed Or calculated, IS to be rounded off, It shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numencal values l revised)'
